text:
ConocoPhillips fell 6.1% today after oil prices dropped on news that a damaged Saudi pipeline will restart operations within days. That pipeline has been crucial as a workaround while the Strait of Hormuz remains contested between the U.S. and Iran; its return to service reduces the supply-shortage premium that had been supporting crude prices. US oil dropped to $107 per barrel today, a sharp pullback from the spike that had driven the stock up $4.55 yesterday.

The broader market context adds complexity: diesel prices hit an all-time high of $6.31 per gallon, which normally supports energy stocks, but the immediate catalyst was geopolitical relief—the easing of one critical chokepoint. ConocoPhillips also sits amid a widening gap between US crude ($107) and global crude ($130.80), suggesting regional supply dynamics are shifting as alternative routes come back online.
